cards.term: What was Aristotle's mistake about motion?
cards.definition: He thought a force is needed to keep a body in uniform motion

cards.term: Why does a real object need a push to keep moving at constant speed?
cards.definition: Only to cancel friction. With no friction, no force is needed

cards.term: What did Galileo's double inclined plane show?
cards.definition: A ball rises to the same height on the other side; make that side flat and it would roll forever

cards.term: What is inertia?
cards.definition: A body's resistance to any change in its state of rest or uniform motion

cards.term: What is the measure of inertia?
cards.definition: Mass

cards.text: Newton's first law: every body continues in its state of {{c1::rest or uniform motion in a straight line}} unless compelled by an {{c2::external force}} to change it.

cards.term: First law in one line?
cards.definition: Net external force = 0 ⇔ acceleration = 0

cards.term: A book rests on a table. What is the correct reasoning?
cards.definition: It is at rest, so net force = 0, so the normal force equals the weight. (Not "forces cancel, so it rests")

cards.term: What external force accelerates a car on a road?
cards.definition: Friction from the road. Internal forces cannot accelerate the car as a whole

cards.term: A bus starts suddenly. Which way are standing passengers thrown, and why?
cards.definition: Backward: friction moves the feet with the bus while the upper body stays at rest (inertia)

cards.term: A bus stops suddenly. Which way are passengers thrown?
cards.definition: Forward (upper body keeps moving)

cards.term: In deep space, a stone is released from a spaceship accelerating at 1 m/s². Acceleration of the stone just after release?
cards.definition: 0. Once released, no force acts on it

cards.term: Define momentum.
cards.definition: \(\vec p = m\vec v\), a vector

cards.term: Why does a cricketer draw the hands back while catching?
cards.definition: To increase the time of stopping the ball, so the force on the hands is smaller

cards.text: Newton's second law: the rate of change of momentum is {{c1::proportional to the applied force}} and takes place {{c2::in the direction of the force}}.

cards.term: Second law as an equation (constant mass)?
cards.definition: \(\vec F = \dfrac{d\vec p}{dt} = m\vec a\)

cards.term: Define 1 newton.
cards.definition: 1 N = 1 kg m s⁻²: the force that gives 1 kg an acceleration of 1 m s⁻²

cards.term: Is the second law a scalar or vector law?
cards.definition: Vector: it holds separately for each component

cards.term: A force acts perpendicular to the velocity. What changes?
cards.definition: Only the direction of velocity, not its magnitude

cards.term: What does 'the second law is a local law' mean?
cards.definition: Acceleration at an instant depends only on the force at that instant, not on past motion

cards.term: Which F and a go into F = ma for a system of particles?
cards.definition: The total external force and the acceleration of the system as a whole

cards.term: Bullet stopped in block: resistive force

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Example 4.2

Find the missing step.

A 0.04 kg bullet at 90 m/s stops after 60 cm in a wooden block. Average resistive force?
  1. v² = u² − 2as with v = 0
  2. a = 90² / (2 × 0.6) = 6750 m s⁻²
  3. ?
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Example 4.2

Find the missing step.

A 0.04 kg bullet at 90 m/s stops after 60 cm in a wooden block. Average resistive force?
  1. v² = u² − 2as with v = 0
  2. a = 90² / (2 × 0.6) = 6750 m s⁻²
  3. F = ma = 0.04 × 6750 = 270 N

cards.term: Define impulse.
cards.definition:
\(J = F\,\Delta t = \Delta p\)
Unit: N s

cards.term: What is an impulsive force?
cards.definition: A large force acting for a very short time (e.g. bat on ball)

cards.term: Why use impulse instead of force for a bat hitting a ball?
cards.definition: Force and contact time are hard to measure separately, but Δp is easy

cards.term: A 0.15 kg ball at 12 m/s is hit straight back at the same speed. Impulse?
A ball of mass m and speed u rebounds from a wall at angle θ to the normal, same speed. Impulse?
cards.definition: 2mu cos θ, along the normal to the wall (parallel component unchanged)

cards.term: State Newton's third law.
cards.definition: To every action there is an equal and opposite reaction: force on A by B = − force on B by A

cards.term: Do action and reaction cancel each other?
cards.definition: No. They act on different bodies

cards.term: Which comes first: action or reaction?
cards.definition: Neither. They are simultaneous; either can be called the action

cards.term: Weight of a book and the normal force on it: action–reaction pair?
cards.definition: No. Both act on the same body (the book)

cards.term: What is the reaction to the Earth's pull on a book?
cards.definition: The book's pull on the Earth (equal, upward)

cards.term: What do the internal action–reaction forces in a body add up to?
cards.definition: Zero

cards.term: State the law of conservation of momentum.
cards.definition: Total momentum of an isolated system (no external force) stays constant

cards.term: Which laws does momentum conservation follow from?
cards.definition: The second and third laws

cards.term: Recoil velocity of a gun (mass M) firing a bullet (mass m, velocity v)?
cards.definition:
\(V = -\dfrac{m v}{M}\)
Opposite to the bullet

cards.term: Is momentum conserved in an inelastic collision?
cards.definition: Yes. Momentum is conserved in all collisions (kinetic energy only in elastic ones)

cards.term: When is a particle in equilibrium?
cards.definition: When the net external force on it is zero

cards.term: Three concurrent forces keep a particle in equilibrium. Geometric condition?
cards.definition: They form a closed triangle when drawn head to tail

cards.term: Lami's theorem for three forces in equilibrium?
cards.definition:
\(\dfrac{F_1}{\sin\alpha} = \dfrac{F_2}{\sin\beta} = \dfrac{F_3}{\sin\gamma}\)
each angle is opposite its force

cards.term: Which two kinds of force appear in mechanics problems?
cards.definition: Gravity (non-contact) and contact forces (normal, friction, tension, spring)

cards.text: The contact force between two surfaces has a component perpendicular to the surface, the {{c1::normal reaction}}, and a component along it, {{c2::friction}}.

cards.term: Hooke's law for a spring?
cards.definition:
\(F = -kx\)
k = spring constant; force opposes the displacement

cards.term: Tension in a massless string over a smooth pulley?
cards.definition: The same at every point

cards.term: What does friction oppose?
cards.definition: Relative motion (actual or impending) between surfaces, not motion itself

cards.term: Why is static friction called self-adjusting?
cards.definition: It grows to match the applied force, up to a maximum

cards.term: Law of static friction?
cards.definition:
\(f_s \le \mu_s N\)
Limiting friction: \(f_{s,\max} = \mu_s N\)

cards.term: Law of kinetic friction?
cards.definition: \(f_k = \mu_k N\)

cards.term: Which is larger: μₛ or μₖ?
cards.definition: μₛ: it is harder to start motion than to keep it going

cards.term: Does friction depend on the area of contact?
cards.definition: No. It depends on N and the nature of the surfaces

cards.term: Static vs kinetic vs rolling friction
cards.definition: Largest: Limiting static friction; Middle: Kinetic (sliding) friction; Smallest: Rolling friction (2–3 orders smaller)

cards.term: Why does rolling friction exist at all?
cards.definition: The surfaces deform slightly, so contact is an area, not a point

cards.term: Three ways to reduce friction?
cards.definition: Lubricants, ball bearings, a cushion of air

cards.term: Three places where friction is needed?
cards.definition: Walking, a car accelerating on a road, brakes

cards.term: Max acceleration of a truck so a box on it does not slide (μₛ)?
cards.definition:
\(a_{\max} = \mu_s g\)
e.g. μₛ = 0.15 → 1.5 m s⁻²

cards.term: A block just starts to slide when the incline reaches angle θ. Relation with μₛ?
cards.definition: \(\tan\theta = \mu_s\) (angle of repose). Independent of mass

cards.term: Acceleration down a rough incline (angle θ, μₖ)?
cards.definition: \(a = g(\sin\theta - \mu_k\cos\theta)\)

cards.term: Why is it easier to pull a roller than to push it (force at an angle)?
cards.definition: Pulling reduces N (mg − F sin θ), so friction is less; pushing increases N

cards.term: Block and trolley: acceleration

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Example 4.9

Find the missing step.

3 kg block hangs from a string over a smooth pulley, pulling a 20 kg trolley (μₖ = 0.04). g = 10 m/s².
  1. Block: 30 − T = 3a
  2. Trolley: T − fk = 20a
  3. fk = μkN = 0.04 × 200 = 8 N
  4. ?
  5. T = 30 − 3a = 27.1 N
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Example 4.9

Find the missing step.

3 kg block hangs from a string over a smooth pulley, pulling a 20 kg trolley (μₖ = 0.04). g = 10 m/s².
  1. Block: 30 − T = 3a
  2. Trolley: T − fk = 20a
  3. fk = μkN = 0.04 × 200 = 8 N
  4. Add: 30 − 8 = 23a → a = 0.96 m s⁻²
  5. T = 30 − 3a = 27.1 N

cards.term: Centripetal force for a body moving in a circle?
cards.definition: \(F = \dfrac{mv^2}{R}\), towards the centre

cards.term: What provides the centripetal force for a stone on a string, a planet, and a car on a level road?
cards.definition: Tension; gravity of the Sun; static friction

cards.term: Max safe speed on a level curve?
cards.definition:
\(v_{\max} = \sqrt{\mu_s R g}\)
Independent of the mass of the car

cards.term: Optimum speed on a banked road (no friction needed)?
cards.definition: \(v_0 = \sqrt{R g \tan\theta}\)

cards.term: Max safe speed on a banked road?
cards.definition: \(v_{\max} = \sqrt{Rg\,\dfrac{\mu_s + \tan\theta}{1 - \mu_s\tan\theta}}\)

cards.term: Why is driving at the optimum speed on a banked road good for tyres?
cards.definition: Friction is not needed, so there is little wear and tear

cards.term: Car on a banked road at v < v₀: which way does friction act?
cards.definition: Up the slope

cards.term: When can a car stay parked on a banked road?
cards.definition: \(\tan\theta \le \mu_s\)

cards.term: Cyclist: 5 m/s on a 3 m turn, μₛ = 0.1, g = 9.8. Slips?
cards.definition: Yes: v² = 25 > μₛRg = 2.94

cards.term: Racetrack R = 300 m, banked 15°. Optimum speed?
cards.definition: 28.1 m s⁻¹ (√(Rg tan θ))

cards.term: Apparent weight in a lift
cards.definition: At rest / uniform velocity: mg; Accelerating up at a: m(g + a); Accelerating down at a: m(g − a); Free fall (a = g): Zero (weightless)

advancedHtml.frontHtml:

Accelerating down at a?

Accelerating up at am(g + a)

cards.term: Atwood machine (m₁ > m₂): acceleration?
Atwood machine: tension in the string?
What is a free-body diagram?
cards.definition: A diagram of the chosen system showing all forces on it from everything else

cards.term: Should a free-body diagram show forces the system exerts on its surroundings?
cards.definition: No

cards.term: If the force on A by B is F in A's free-body diagram, what goes in B's?
cards.definition: \(-\vec F\) (third law)

cards.term: Block and cylinder sinking: normal force

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Example 4.12

Find the missing step.

A 2 kg block and a 25 kg cylinder on it sink together at 0.1 m/s² into a soft floor. g = 10 m/s². Force of the floor?
  1. Weight of system = 27 × 10 = 270 N
  2. 270 − R′ = 27 × 0.1
  3. ?
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Example 4.12

Find the missing step.

A 2 kg block and a 25 kg cylinder on it sink together at 0.1 m/s² into a soft floor. g = 10 m/s². Force of the floor?
  1. Weight of system = 27 × 10 = 270 N
  2. 270 − R′ = 27 × 0.1
  3. R′ = 267.3 N
